title: Seat the casting ring that leaves 5-8 mm over a wax crown, never touching the wax
instruction: Three steel casting rings stand on the left of the table. Pick the one whose top edge will be 5 to 8 mm above the top of the blue wax crown once the ring stands on the black former. Lower it straight down over the crown and stand it on the former around the raised step, then let go. Leave the other two rings off the former. Never let a ring or a gripper touch the wax crown or its red sprue.
context: Dental laboratory technicians (O*NET 51-9081.00) cast crowns and inlays by the lost-wax method. The sprued wax pattern stands on a rubber crucible former, and the technician sets a casting ring over it so that about 6 mm of investment will cover the pattern (Phillips' Science of Dental Materials). Much less and the mould end cracks or the metal breaks through; much more and the gases cannot escape (back-pressure porosity). The ring must not touch the pattern, because inlay wax dents under the lightest touch and a touched pattern is waxed up again, and it is seated on the former so the investment cannot leak. The core of the task is that contact-free placement: a sleeve lowered straight down round a fragile part it then hides, judged at every step. Choosing it by the cover it will leave comes first; unlike choosing a pin, a block or a support by fit or height, the chosen part must then pass round another part without touching it.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Seven things are on the table. (1) Crucible former base: a black rubber block 88 x 88 x 10 mm, fixed to the table, centred at x 30.0 cm, y +8.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y (a square stand-in for a round former). Its centre line is the former's axis. (2) Centring step: a black rubber disc 36 mm across and 6 mm tall, fixed on the base's top, centred on the former's axis (its top 16 mm above the table). (3) Sprue: a red wax rod 4 mm across and 10 mm tall, fixed upright on the step with its axis at x 30.0 cm, y +8.6 cm (6 mm left of the former's axis), from 16 to 26 mm above the table. (4) Wax crown: a blue inlay wax block standing in for a crown pattern, 10 x 12 x 10 mm (10 mm along x, 12 mm along y, 10 mm tall), fixed on top of the sprue and centred on its axis (x 29.5 to 30.5 cm, y +8.0 to +9.2 cm), from 26 to 36 mm above the table; its top is 36 mm above the table. (5)-(7) Three loose grey stainless-steel casting rings, each a square tube open at both ends, 60 x 60 mm outside with 4 mm walls (a 52 x 52 mm opening), standing upright on the table with their sides parallel to x and y: ring A, 40 mm tall, 0.28 kg, centred at x 20.0 cm, y +33.0 cm; ring B, 24 mm tall, 0.17 kg, centred at x 29.0 cm, y +32.0 cm; ring C, 32 mm tall, 0.23 kg, centred at x 39.0 cm, y +29.0 cm. Nothing but their heights tells them apart. Stood on the former's base (10 mm up) their tops would be 50, 34 and 42 mm above the table: 14 mm above, 2 mm below and 6 mm above the crown's top, so ring C is the one that leaves 5 to 8 mm. Centred on the former's axis, a ring's inner walls clear the step by 8 mm on every side and the crown by 14 mm (on the +y side) to 26 mm. Gripping from above, only the left arm reaches the rings; both arms reach the former. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial, once per control step (20 Hz): each ring's pose and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point (between the tips), opening (0 closed, 1 open: pads 94 mm apart) and turn about its axis. A ring may be either way up (it is open at both ends): its tilt is its axis's angle from vertical (0 to 90 degrees) and its lower end is whichever end is lower. Touching the wax means, at any moment, (a) a wall of any ring (its real 4 mm wall, posed as the ring is) within 0.5 mm of the crown or of a 4 x 4 mm square post round the sprue; or (b) a point of the crown's or the sprue's surface inside a finger: each finger is a box 10 mm thick outside the gap, 40 mm wide and 70 mm long from the tips up, posed as the gripper is and grown 1 mm on every side. On a step where a gripper's turn cannot be read, its boxes are swept round its axis (any turn): from half the gap less 1 mm to sqrt((half the gap + 11 mm)^2 + (21 mm)^2) from the axis, from 1 mm below the tips to 71 mm above them. 'Over the wax': tilted 10 degrees or less, every corner of the crown and of the sprue post inside the ring's 52 x 52 mm opening (in the ring's own frame), and the crown's top above the ring's lower end. 'Held': a gripper's fingers are under 88 mm apart (a grip across the ring's corners stops at 84.9 mm) and its tip point is below the ring's top and within 45 mm of the ring's axis horizontally. 'Still': the ring's centre moved 2 mm or less in total over the last 0.5 s. 'Seated': over the wax, all four outer corners of its lower end 9 to 12 mm above the table (on the base, whose top is 10 mm up, not on the step, 16 mm up; this also means tilted under 3 degrees), not held, and still. 'On the former': a ring's centre within 45 mm of the former's axis seen from above, or a point of its lower end's outer edge (sampled every 5 mm) above the base's 88 x 88 mm outline and 5 mm or more above the table (leaning on the base, resting on another ring there, or held over it). Score 0 if the wax was touched at any moment, whatever follows; or if at the end two or more rings are on the former; or if the grippers could not be read on more than 1% of the steps (on such a step rule (b) is skipped and every ring counts as held). Otherwise: 1.0 if ring C (32 mm) is seated; 0.5 if ring C is over the wax but not seated (still held, hovering, crooked, resting on the step's edge, or moving); 0.25 if ring A (40 mm) or ring B (24 mm) is seated; 0 in every other case (no ring over the wax, a wrong ring over the wax but not seated, nothing done). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. The score is read at the last step; the trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2.5 s. In a real trial: inlay wax shows a touch as a dent or smear, and video from above and two sides shows any finger touch; a 2 mm feeler gauge must not pass under any corner of the ring's lower edge (seated); a straightedge across the ring's top and a depth gauge down to the crown's top read the cover; count the rings standing on, leaning on or held over the former.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The rings are square steel tubes (four 4 mm walls) standing in for round rings; there is no ring liner and no investment is poured. The former is a square rubber block with a round step. The wax is fixed and cannot dent, so a touch is judged from geometry: ring walls as they are, fingers as boxes at least as big as the real ones, posed as the gripper is. The gripper's body above the fingers and the arm are not judged.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed in simulation. Stand the three rings back upright on their start spots, sides parallel to x and y: ring A at x 20.0 cm, y +33.0 cm; ring B at x 29.0 cm, y +32.0 cm; ring C at x 39.0 cm, y +29.0 cm. The former, sprue and crown are fixed. In a real build check the wax for dents after each trial and remake the pattern if it was touched.
